hook.text: France and Poland had an alliance in 1939. When Germany invaded Poland, France barely moved. Allies froze.

buildup.text: Alliances fail when the cost of honoring them exceeds the cost of breaking them. Paper commitments bend under fire.

discovery.text: Credibility is the currency of alliances. Once you fail one partner, every other partner questions your word.

twist.text: The US withdrawal from Afghanistan in 2021 rattled allies worldwide. If America leaves there, who's next?

climax.text: Alliance failure cascades. When one ally doubts your resolve, it hedges. That hedging weakens the entire network.

punchline.text: An alliance is only as strong as its worst test.

quiz.question: What happens to alliance networks when one commitment fails?
options: Other members increase their own defense spending
Other partners doubt credibility and begin hedging
New alliances form immediately to fill the gap
